_about: Question each Better Boulder questionnaire statement answers. Matched against the published pages on 2026-10-13 (betterboulder.com/2026-city-council-candidate-questionnaire and /where-do-boulder-2026-mayorial-candidates-ctand/). Used by build_chat_context.py so a bare 'Yes.'/'No.' is never shown without its question. Re-checked 2026-10-13: S-benita-duran-2 and S-tina-marquis-1 ('Yes. No additional comment submitted.', topic transportation) answer the Core Arterial Network question, not the duplex ordinance. Oct. 13: tools/approve_2026.py (RESTORED_QUESTIONNAIRE_ANSWERS) adds seven answers the research harvest dropped (four Core Arterial Network 'Yes. No additional comment submitted.' answers, Schuchard's DDA answer, Fuqua's and Marquis's priorities answers) and maps them here.

prompts.S-taishya-adams-1: In early 2025, the Boulder City Council passed an ordinance called Family-Friendly Vibrant Neighborhoods to make it easier to build duplexes and triplexes in single-family home neighborhoods. Would you have voted yes or no on that ordinance? [If you were on city council when this vote occurred, did you vote to make it easier to build duplexes and triplexes?]
prompts.S-taishya-adams-2: Are you committed to the build out of the Core Arterial Network?
prompts.S-taishya-adams-3: The City is exploring the creation of a Downtown Development Authority (DDA) to increase investment in our downtown area. Is this the right path for revitalizing downtown Boulder? What do you view as the pros and cons? Are there alternative approaches to improving the economic vitality of downtown Boulder that you are interested in exploring?
prompts.S-taishya-adams-4: Acknowledging that the job of governing requires skillful navigation of competing priorities, what do you think are the city government’s current top three priorities? What do you think their top three priorities should be?
